deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a reading excerpt in Riemann's hand from Herbart, Sämmtliche Werke vol. VI (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 2nd analytic part, 2nd section, ch. 3 'Von unserer Auffassung der Welt und den damit verbundenen Täuschungen', §139, pp. 260–263). The surrounding pages continue the same reading (Locke on the accidental aggregate of qualities, Leibniz, §§140–141).

The excerpted argument runs as follows.

(1) Distinct thinking means taking a concept apart into its marks ('Auseinandersetzen', underlined by Riemann). Herbart wants this taken literally: it includes estimating, even measuring, the degree of difference between two compared marks. His examples are degrees of heat read on a thermometer and of heaviness read by weight.

(2) To account for this, Herbart introduces 'Reihenformen' (serial forms). These are kinds of representation comparable to space and time.

(3) Space arises from graded fusions ('abgestufte Verschmelzungen') of representations. So whenever a class of simple representations, present together in consciousness, fuses in degrees fixed by their quality, they order themselves 'beside and between one another'. One then necessarily describes them in spatial language, which in fact belongs to the series just as originally as to space. Examples are tones and colours. The principle, underlined by Riemann: the greater the degree of mutual inhibition, the smaller the fusion.

(4) Logical classification is exact only insofar as its specific differences form definite serial forms (library, botanical system).

(5) A thing is a complex of marks. Once each mark is placed in its own qualitative continuum (colour among colours, tone among tones, weight on the scale of heaviness), two things follow:
- the complex decomposes into its marks;
- comparing two things yields, for each pair of marks of the same class, a determinate measurable distance on that continuum.
Examples: the difference in specific gravity of two metals, the interval between their sounds, the distance of their colours on a colour chart.

(6) Herbart uses only the first consequence. The marks appear as a contingent aggregate. Gold could have had another specific gravity, ductility or fusibility. Seeing the whole continua, one sees the actual thing 'in the midst of other possibilities', and experience reveals its contingency.

In modern terms, the mathematically relevant content is this: a thing is represented as a point in a product of several one-dimensional qualitative continua, with a distance defined coordinate-wise on each continuum. This is a proto-notion of a multiply extended manifold whose points are determined by several continuous qualitative coordinates. This Herbartian background is generally cited as feeding into Riemann's 1854 Habilitation lecture. That lecture gives positions of sensory objects and colours as examples of multiply extended magnitudes, and it explicitly acknowledges Herbart. There is no derivation to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible: there is no computation. The content is philosophical-psychological excerpting.

Philosophically, Herbart's claim that each pair of marks gives a measurable 'Auseinander' presupposes, without justification, that every qualitative continuum carries a metric. Riemann's 1854 lecture is precisely careful to separate extension (manifold structure) from measure relations (metric). Herbart's colour-chart distance is also not a well-defined metric.

results.what: Herbart's 'Reihenformen': qualitative continua (tones, colours, degrees of weight/heat) ordered by graded fusion, described in spatial language, with things as aggregates of positions in several such continua
results.modern_name: Precursor of the notion of an n-dimensional manifold / feature space (product of 1-dimensional continua); colour space
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 1824–25); its influence on Riemann's 1854 Habilitation lecture 'Über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen'

results.what: Riemann's reading notes on Herbart Werke VI §139 (pp. 260–263)
results.modern_name: Documentary evidence of Herbart's influence on Riemann's manifold concept
results.usually_credited_to: Discussed by E. Scholz (Historia Mathematica 1982, 'Herbart's influence on Bernhard Riemann'), L. Boi, J. Ferreirós and others; Riemann himself named Herbart as an influence

deep.surprise_reason: These are excerpts from Herbart, not original mathematics. Herbart's influence on Riemann's manifold concept, including the Reihenformen and colour/tone examples, is well documented and acknowledged by Riemann himself. The page is a confirming detail of known reading, of modest archival interest only.
transcription_corrections: Line after '§. 139.': the image reads '..wir müssten nun das Geschäft, die Formen der Erfahrung nach ihren Ursprüngen psychologisch zu erklären, vollends zu Ende bringen' ('das Geschäft', not 'deshalb[?]').

'die Grade der Wärme und Kälte nach dem Thermometer, die der Schwere nach dem Gewicht' — 'die der Schwere' is correct as transcribed; the passage before it is 'welcher Ausdruck hier so wörtlich als möglich zu nehmen ist'.
p. 262 opening: probably 'Da der Raum auf abgestuften Verschmelzungen beruht' (causal 'Da', as in Herbart's text) rather than 'Wo'.
Example sentence on p. 263: 'die sammt ihrer Distanz auf der Farbentafel können nachgewiesen werden' is more likely than 'die zusammen[?] ihre Distanz'.
'als ein Aggregat' is confirmed by the next page ('zufälliges Aggregat'); the '[?]' can be removed.

Underlinings in the manuscript: 'deutlichen', 'Auseinandersetzen', 'neben' and 'zwischen', 'Je grösser der Hemmungsgrad, desto geringer die Verschmelzung', 'in einem andern', 'als zufällig beisammen'.
Deleted words in 'überhaupt alle [Farben] [aus einer] Merkmale aus einerlei Classe' are correctly marked as cancellations; the 'aus einer' deletion is better read as 'und andere' (uncertain).
Archival stamp '56' (folio number) in the right margin is not part of the text.
